entries.claim: App registration starts at Identity > Applications > App registrations > New registration
entries.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/auth-register-app-v2 "Browse to Identity > Applications > App registrations and select New registration."

entries.claim: Client secret lifetime is limited to a maximum of 24 months
entries.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/auth-register-app-v2 "Client secret lifetime is limited to two years (24 months) or less." Microsoft also recommends less than 12 months.

entries.claim: Redirect URIs are added on the Redirect URI configuration tab under Authentication
entries.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/how-to-add-redirect-uri "On the Redirect URI configuration tab, select Add Redirect URI."

entries.claim: SPA redirect URIs must be set to type spa using the application manifest editor
entries.before: SPA redirect URIs must be set to type spa using the application manifest editor.
entries.after: New SPA redirect URIs are added by choosing the Single-page application platform on the Authentication page. The manifest editor is only one way to change an existing URI's type to spa.
entries.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/how-to-add-redirect-uri "Single-page application | Enter a Redirect URI for client-side apps using JavaScript, Angular, React.js"

entries.claim: Admin-restricted permissions like Directory.ReadWrite.All require Global Administrator consent
entries.before: Admin-restricted permissions require Global Administrator consent.
entries.after: Admin-restricted permissions need tenant-wide admin consent. For delegated permissions this can come from a Cloud Application Administrator, Application Administrator, AI Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator. Microsoft Graph application permissions (app roles) need a Privileged Role Administrator. Global Administrator is not the only role that can grant it.
entries.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/grant-admin-consent "Cloud Application Administrator, AI Administrator, or Application Administrator, for granting consent for apps requesting any permission for any API, except Microsoft Graph app roles"

entries.claim: offline_access is requested to obtain a refresh token
entries.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/v2-oauth2-auth-code-flow "refresh_token ... Note: Only provided if offline_access scope was requested."

entries.claim: The authorization code is redeemed by POST to the /token endpoint
entries.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/v2-oauth2-auth-code-flow "Redeem the code by sending a POST request to the /token endpoint"

entries.claim: Publisher verification requires a Partner One ID for a verified Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program account
entries.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/publisher-verification-overview "The CPP account must be the partner global account (PGA) for the developer's organization." Location Partner One IDs are not supported.

entries.claim: Apps to be publisher verified must be registered with a Microsoft Entra work or school account
entries.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/publisher-verification-overview "Apps that are registered by using a Microsoft account can't be publisher verified."

entries.claim: Users can't consent to most newly registered unverified multitenant apps when risk-based step-up consent applies
entries.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/configure-risk-based-step-up-consent "the request requires a "step-up" to admin consent instead. This step-up capability is enabled by default". It applies to apps registered after Nov 8, 2020 that request more than basic sign-in and profile permissions from users in other tenants.

entries.claim: A blue verified badge appears on the consent prompt after publisher verification
entries.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/publisher-verification-overview "a blue verified badge appears in the Microsoft Entra consent prompt for the app"

entries.claim: Microsoft does not charge for publisher verification
entries.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/publisher-verification-overview "Microsoft doesn't charge developers for publisher verification. No license is required"

entries.claim: Client credentials flow needs an Application ID URI as scope (labelled sourced)
entries.method: Read the cited URL type (learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers Q&A thread) on 2026-11-01
entries.after: label: community. The source is a Microsoft Q&A forum answer, not product documentation, and the guide's OAuth user flow does not depend on this claim.
entries.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/1502925/do-i-need-a-redirect-uri-when-using-a-windows-app (Microsoft Q&A community forum thread, not a docs page)

entries.claim: Scope Mail.Read: triggersReview false; 'subject to user or admin consent depending on tenant policies'
entries.before: Mail.Read can be granted by user or admin consent depending on tenant policies.
entries.after: Under the Microsoft-managed consent policy, which is the default for new tenants, end users cannot consent to Mail.Read, Calendars.*, Files.Read.All, Sites.Read.All, Chat.* and similar permissions. A tenant admin must grant consent, even if the app is publisher verified. No Microsoft review is involved.
entries.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/manage-app-consent-policies "This is also the default for a new tenant... End users can consent for any user consentable delegated permissions EXCEPT" (list includes Mail.Read)

entries.after: triggersReview: false. No Microsoft scope triggers a review by Microsoft. Directory.ReadWrite.All needs tenant admin consent in every customer tenant, which is a customer-side limit and not a provider review.
entries.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/grant-admin-consent "Granting tenant-wide admin consent requires you to sign in as a user that is authorized to consent on behalf of the organization."

entries.claim: verdict.approvalWait 1-5 days; gap: CPP verification processing time unknown
entries.before: approvalWait 1-5 days; CPP verification time listed as a gap
entries.after: Partner Center account verification usually takes 3-5 business days (about 3-7 calendar days) and can take longer. After that, marking the app as publisher verified takes minutes.
entries.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/partner-center/enroll/understand-the-verification-process "In most cases, the process takes three to five business days to complete."

entries.claim: Publisher domain must match the CPP-verified domain (requirements.domain)
entries.before: Publisher domain must match the domain verified under the CPP account.
entries.after: The CPP verification email domain must match the app's publisher domain or a DNS-verified custom domain on the tenant. The publisher domain cannot be *.onmicrosoft.com. The tenant must be associated with the partner global account (PGA). The user who verifies needs MFA plus an Application Admin or Cloud Application Admin role, and a CPP Partner Admin or Account Admin role.
entries.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/publisher-verification-overview "the app's publisher domain can't be *.onmicrosoft.com to be publisher verified"

entries.claim: Redirect URIs must use https except some localhost URIs
entries.method: Attempted cross-check via https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/how-to-add-redirect-uri on 2026-11-01 (reply-url page not fetched)
entries.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/how-to-add-redirect-uri gives the example "http://localhost:3000/auth-response if you run your app locally", which is consistent but not a direct quote of the rule

verdict.topBlocker: Customer tenants on Microsoft's default consent policy block end-user consent for mail, calendar, files and chat scopes, so a tenant admin must grant consent even after publisher verification.
verdict.summary: The only wait is Partner Center verification of your AI Cloud Partner Program account (usually 3-5 business days); after that, publisher verification takes minutes and lets users in other tenants consent without the risky-app step-up. Marketplace/AppSource, the Entra app gallery and Microsoft 365 App Compliance are optional; the real limit is that customer-tenant consent policies often require an admin to approve agent-style scopes such as Mail.Read.
verdict.reason: Moved approvalWait from 1-5 to 3-7 days, using Microsoft's official 3-5 business-day Partner Center estimate. Raised effort because CPP enrollment needs business, domain and identity documents plus a DNS-verified publisher domain. Changed topBlocker from 'unverified publisher' to tenant admin consent: Microsoft's managed default policy excludes Mail/Calendar/Files/Chat scopes from user consent whatever the publisher status. Difficulty stays at 3.

optionalPaths.name: Microsoft Marketplace (AppSource) SaaS offer
optionalPaths.why: For publishers who want discovery or to sell through Microsoft. It is not needed for OAuth; Microsoft documents automated steps in minutes but gives no duration for the manual certification phase.
optionalPaths.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/partner-center/marketplace-offers/review-publish-offer "Offers submitted to Microsoft Marketplace must be certified before being published."

optionalPaths.name: Microsoft 365 App Compliance - Publisher Attestation
optionalPaths.why: A self-service security questionnaire, renewed yearly, that produces a public docs page for enterprise security reviewers; useful when customer admins will be asked to grant mail or files consent.
optionalPaths.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365-app-certification/docs/certification "Publisher Attestation is a self-service process where app developers (ISVs) complete a set of questions about their security practices"

optionalPaths.name: Microsoft 365 Certification
optionalPaths.why: A paid audit through Claranet (pentest if none in the last 12 months) for selling to security-strict enterprises; the ISV gets a 14-day window for initial documents and 60 days (+60 discretionary) for evidence, but no total review time is stated.
optionalPaths.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365-app-certification/docs/certification "ISV will work with audit firm to pay for the certification."

optionalPaths.name: Microsoft Entra App Gallery listing
optionalPaths.why: Only for SaaS vendors who want SSO (SAML/OIDC) or SCIM provisioning to show up in customers' Enterprise apps gallery; needs a Partner One ID and isn't needed for Graph OAuth.
optionalPaths.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/publisher-verification-overview "Is publisher verification the same as the Microsoft Entra application gallery? No."

limits.limit: The Microsoft-managed default user consent policy (default for new tenants) excludes Mail.*, Calendars.*, Files.Read(Write).All, Sites.Read(Write).All, Chat.*, Contacts.*, Tasks.*, People.Read and others from end-user consent
limits.impact: An email, calendar or files agent cannot be self-connected by ordinary users in most tenants, so your onboarding must route customers to a tenant admin through the admin consent URL or the admin consent workflow.
limits.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/manage-app-consent-policies "End users can consent for any user consentable delegated permissions EXCEPT"

limits.limit: Risk-based step-up consent (on by default) turns user consent into an admin requirement for unverified multitenant apps that ask for more than basic permissions
limits.impact: Without publisher verification even low-risk scopes beyond sign-in/profile fail with AADSTS90094 for users in other tenants, which makes publisher verification practically required.
limits.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/configure-risk-based-step-up-consent "This step-up capability is enabled by default, but it results in a behavior change only when user consent is enabled."

limits.limit: Tenants can disable user consent, or allow it only for verified publishers and low-impact permissions (microsoft-user-default-low)
limits.impact: Some customers will never allow user consent, so the agent must support an admin-consent-first onboarding path.
limits.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/configure-user-consent "Allow limited user consent only for apps from verified publishers and apps that are registered in your tenant"

limits.limit: Microsoft Graph application permissions (app roles) can only be granted by a Privileged Role Administrator; apps with assignment required always need admin consent
limits.impact: Background or daemon agent access to all mailboxes needs a highly privileged customer admin to approve it, which slows sales.
limits.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/enterprise-apps/grant-admin-consent "Privileged Role Administrator, for granting consent for apps requesting any permission, for any API."

limits.limit: Refresh tokens last 90 days by default (24 hours for SPA redirect URIs) and can be revoked by password reset or admin action
limits.impact: A long-running agent must use a confidential (web) client, rotate refresh tokens, and handle invalid_grant by asking the user to reconnect.
limits.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/refresh-tokens "24 hours for single-page applications... 90 days for all other scenarios."

limits.limit: Outlook throttling: 10,000 requests per 10 minutes and 4 concurrent requests per app per mailbox; 130,000 requests per 10 seconds per app across all tenants; 429 with Retry-After
limits.impact: An agent that scans mail has to use delta queries or change notifications and honour Retry-After, not poll.
limits.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/throttling-limits "10,000 API requests in a 10-minute period | v1.0 and beta endpoints"

limits.limit: Client secrets expire after at most 24 months (12 months or less recommended)
limits.impact: Plan secret rotation or use certificates, or every customer connection breaks when the secret expires.
limits.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/auth-register-app-v2 "You can't specify a custom lifetime longer than 24 months."

stepChanges.newTitle: Create a multitenant App Registration from a work/school account
stepChanges.newDetail: In the Microsoft Entra admin center (Identity > Applications > App registrations > New registration), choose 'Accounts in any organizational directory' (optionally plus personal Microsoft accounts) so that other companies' users can connect. Register it from a work or school (Entra) account, because apps registered with a personal Microsoft account can't be publisher verified.
stepChanges.reason: The guide doesn't say that multitenant is required for any customer to connect, or that the account type decides whether the app can be verified later.

stepChanges.newDetail: Under Certificates & secrets, upload a certificate (recommended for production) or create a client secret. Secrets last at most 24 months and Microsoft recommends under 12, so plan rotation. Copy the secret value right away; it isn't shown again.
stepChanges.reason: Microsoft recommends certificates or federated credentials for production and caps secret lifetime.

stepChanges.newDetail: Add the Microsoft Graph delegated permissions under API permissions, plus openid, profile and offline_access. Note that Mail.*, Calendars.*, Files.Read.All, Sites.Read.All and Chat.* can't be user-consented in tenants on the Microsoft-managed default policy, so a tenant admin must consent. Avoid Directory.ReadWrite.All and application permissions unless they are truly needed.
stepChanges.reason: The guide says Mail.Read is user-consentable; Microsoft's default consent policy excludes it.

stepChanges.newTitle: Test cross-tenant user consent and admin consent
stepChanges.newDetail: Sign in from a second Entra tenant (not your home tenant) to see the real consent experience, including risk-based step-up. Test the admin consent URL https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/adminconsent?client_id={client-id} and the customer's admin consent workflow request path.
stepChanges.reason: Step-up and default-policy blocks only show up for users outside the tenant where the app is registered.

stepChanges.newTitle: Enroll in Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program (partner global account)
stepChanges.newDetail: Enroll in the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program in Partner Center as the partner global account (PGA), not a location account. Use a business email whose domain matches a DNS-verified custom domain on your Entra tenant, and associate the tenant with the PGA. Have business registration documents and domain registrar documents ready, and complete identity verification.
stepChanges.reason: Required for publisher verification. The guide leaves out the PGA-only rule, the tenant association, and the documents Partner Center verifies.

stepChanges.newTitle: Wait for Partner Center account verification (usually 3-5 business days)
stepChanges.newDetail: Microsoft checks the email, identity, employment (domain documentation) and business registration. Watch Account settings > Legal info > Verification Summary and answer any document requests quickly. Only the primary contact receives the emails.
stepChanges.reason: Microsoft publishes an official 3-5 business-day estimate, which the guide had listed as a gap.

stepChanges.newTitle: Mark the app as publisher verified
stepChanges.newDetail: Sign in with MFA as an Application Admin or Cloud Application Admin who is also a CPP Partner Admin or Account Admin. Set a non-onmicrosoft.com publisher domain, open Branding & properties, choose Add Partner ID to verify publisher, and enter the PGA Partner One ID. This takes minutes; then check the blue badge using prompt=consent.
stepChanges.reason: The guide leaves out the role, MFA and publisher-domain prerequisites that make verification fail.
